newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian bond to be priced slightly over mkt level.
newsitem.headline: Russian bond to be priced slightly over mkt level.

text.p: The record-high volume of government paper to be auctioned on Wednesday combined with the first paper to be repaid ahead of maturity date will prevent yields from falling to their record-low levels they have reached recently, dealers said on Tuesday.

But they said banks will only get a small yield spread over market levels on the GKO discount Treasury bill due to heavy repayment volumes, while the discount on the OFZ bond will depend on how much the Finance Ministry will manage to repay of the 24010 OFZ bond issue, which it will repay on a voluntary basis.
ON WEDNESDAY
The Finance Ministry sells
*12.00 trln rbls 728-day OFZ (series 24014)
*8.00 trln rbls 364-day T-bills (series 21076)
The Finance Ministry pays/repays
*7.12 trln rbls 245-day T-bill (series 22054)
*1.25 trln rbls in interest on OFZ bond (series 24010)
*6.65 trln rbls on series 24010 OFZ bond
ON TUESDAY
*Average rose to 20.2 pct from 20.1 pct on Monday
*Turnover rose to 4.92 trln rbls from 4.37 trln rbls
*Central Bank sold 240 bln rbls in T-bills

Dealers forecast the average yield on series 21076 T-bill would be in the 20.47-21.60 percent range. The series 21075 bill, maturing on June 10, 1998, the closest maturity date to the new issue, closed at 83.35 to yield 20.37 percent.

Dealers forecast the average price on series 24014 OFZ bond would be in the 20.62-20.85 percent range. The series 24013, maturing on May 26, 1999, the closest maturity date to the new issue, closed at 100.68 to yield 24.57 percent.

"This auction is not like any other, when you know the volume of repayment beforehand," a dealer said. "In this case it will be more difficult to calculate the Finance Ministry's payment balance. And as it is not clear how much will be repaid, it is difficult to evaluate the volume of the demand."
On Wednesday the Central Bank will also sell selected OFZ bonds at average prices after the auctions to satisfy any possible demand.
Dealers said that as banks would be able to buy the new OFZ bond issue after the auction at an average price, most banks would put agressive bids for the auction.

"The Finance Ministry was very wise in announcing a trading session," said Moscow Narodny Bank dealer Andrei Vetrov. "Theoretically the bids on OFZ bond could be superagressive and the Central Bank will have to cut most of it. The huge unsatisfied demand could shift to Thursday and hit the market."
One dealer said most of the 24010 bond was held by the Central Bank and state-owned Sberbank, and the Finance Ministry could ignore aggressive bids.

"The new OFZ in neutral investment-wise as its rate is in line with the market rates," Vetrov said. "But it is long and bears interest-rate risk and it should be placed with a discount. So it will be wise to bid aggressively at the auction and if the bid is ignored, to buy at an average price later."
The first coupon rate on the bond is 19.73 percent to be paid on December 17, 1997.
Dealers gave mixed opinions of how much of the 24010 issue would be repaid.

"For active operators it is profitable to get rid of the paper now, as it was bought at prices lower than the face value," Vetrov said. "The tax to be paid later on taxable bonds will be handsomely compensated by the profit from the early repayment due to the difference in buying and repayment prices."
A dealer said the 364-day T-bill would be sold at average market price.
--Anna Smirnova, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
